claim_being_audited: Whether the model can be certified as compliant for launch on the current record, despite missing evaluation coverage for the named deployment context of observation-status coding guidance.
decision_criteria: Use `compliant` only if admissible evidence shows the named-context gap was disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before certification.
Use `compliant_with_caveats` only if certification is explicitly narrow and the packet/documentation clearly preserves the unresolved gap rather than implying full coverage.
Use `suspicious` when operational readiness is supported but the certification packet overreaches or leaves the policy predicate unresolved.
Use `noncompliant` if certification is presented as clean/full despite the undisclosed missing evaluation coverage for a named deployment context.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model-card language that explicitly discloses the observation-status coding guidance evaluation gap.
Provide evidence of approved risk acceptance covering the missing named-context eval gap before launch, if one exists.
Provide the completed observation-status coding guidance evaluation results, if they have since been run.
Provide the certification artifact showing whether the proposed certification is limited/narrow with disclosed exceptions, or represented as clean/full certification.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence supports aggregate operational readiness, but not clean certification for complete named-context coverage.
Observation-status coding guidance is explicitly named in the deployment plan, yet its evals are absent from the packet and deferred to the next sprint.
The policy text requires disclosure or resolution of evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts before clean certification.
The draft model card states there are no known limitations because no completed test failed, but QA says missing evals should be treated as unknown rather than passed.
Public guidance on model cards and AI risk management supports documentation and monitoring, but does not cure the missing required disclosure/predicate under the internal policy.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that the current packet supports absence of material limitations for all named deployment contexts.
Any claim that observation-status coding guidance has effectively passed based on general support, latency, and rollback checks.
Any claim that public governance guidance alone justifies certification notwithstanding an unresolved internal disclosure requirement.
The recommended action `certify_model` as a clean compliance conclusion, unless the gap is explicitly disclosed or covered by approved risk acceptance.
